Returns a Simulation class object.

The simulation a lightcone is built from:

  • a Simulation given as simulation (or as boxsize_resolution, the first argument of the lightcone classes),

  • made from boxsize_resolution and simulation_name (see simulations.Simulation.from_label)

Transform inputs into swiftlet.simulations object and acts as wrapper.

  • simulation_name (str) – name of the simulation, e.g. “HYDRO_FIDUCIAL”

  • simulation_suite_name (str) – “flamingo” or “colibre”. If None, found from boxsize_resolution

swiftlet.snapshot_lightcone.define_redshift_at_comoving_distance_function(cosmo, zmin=0.0001, zmax=5.05, n_grid=3000, method='precise')[source]

Build an interpolation function for the redshift at a given comoving distance.

Returns a CubicSpline function taking comoving distance [Mpc] and returning redshift.

Parameters:

  • cosmo (SnapshotCosmology, astropy cosmology or str) – cosmology of the simulation

  • zmin (float) – minimum redshift of the grid

  • zmax (float) – maximum redshift of the grid

  • n_grid (int) – number of points in the grid

  • method (str) –

    ‘fast’, a uniform grid in redshift, requires less computations now, but few % loss in precision when interpolating later on. ‘precise’, a uniform grid in comoving distance, more transforms required now

    but less of a drop in precision when interpolating later on

swiftlet.snapshot_lightcone.write_halo_lightcone_file(filename, haloes, soap_filename, properties, metadata, nside=16, order='nest')[source]

Write the halo lightcone data to a .hdf5 file.

Write haloes placed in a lightcone to a .hdf5 file in the format of the lightcone_io (FLAMINGO) halo lightcones, so lightcone_io.halo_reader.HaloLightconeFile can read it:

Parameters:

  • filename (str) – path of the HDF5 file to write, e.g. lightcone_haloes_0127.hdf5

  • haloes (dict) – haloes placed by place_haloes_in_shell, all of them on this rank

  • soap_filename (str) – SOAP catalogue of the haloes’ snapshot, for the unit attributes and the Cosmology and Units groups

  • properties (dict) – {name: values} of SOAP properties of each halo to write, e.g. {“InputHalos/IsCentral”: …}

  • metadata (dict) – .metadata of the haloes placed, see SnapshotLightcone.lightcone_metadata

  • nside (int) – HEALPix resolution of the index, as lightcone_io uses (16)

  • order (str) – HEALPix pixel ordering of the index, “nest” or “ring”

class swiftlet.snapshot_lightcone.SnapshotAllSky(simulation_object=None, simulation_suite_name=None, boxsize_resolution=None, simulation_name=None, simulation_base_dir_format=None, orientation_seed=0, orientation_lock=None, orientation_table=None, verbose=1)[source]

Bases: SnapshotLightcone

Class for constructing an all-sky lightcone from snapshots.

Define the all-sky lightcone, passed to SnapshotLightcone with no beam vector.

Parameters:

  • simulation_suite_name (str) – “flamingo” or “colibre”. If None, found from boxsize_resolution

  • simulation_object (Simulation object (swiftlet class object, see swiftlet.simulation_suites)) – the simulation, can be passed instead of boxsize_resolution and simulation_name

  • boxsize_resolution (str or Simulation) – box size and resolution label, e.g. “L1000N1800” (FLAMINGO) or “L0200N1504” (COLIBRE), or a Simulation (see swiftlet.simulations), then pass the other arguments by keyword

  • simulation_name (str) – name of the simulation, e.g. “HYDRO_FIDUCIAL”

  • orientation_seed (int) – seed used to select the rotation, reflection and periodic shift of each box tile

  • verbose (int) – amount printed. 0: nothing, only warnings. 1: a summary of each call. 2: details of every snapshot, box tile and file

  • orientation_lock (str) –

    “none”:

    every box tile has its own orientation.

    ”cube”:
    every box tile in a cube shell of boxes around the observer’s box shares

    one orientation, so each shell is periodically continuous and the orientation only changes on the faces between shells.

    ”sphere”:

    everything in a spherical shell, between (n-1/2) and (n+1/2) box sidelengths from the observer, shares one orientation, so the orientation only changes at those distances. A box crossing a sphere is used once for each shell, and tiles are labelled (nx, ny, nz, layer)

  • simulation_base_dir_format (str) – directory of the simulation, with {box_res} and {sim_name} fields. If None, the suite’s directory (see simulations.SimulationSuite.directory_format)

lightcone_diameter(z, cosmo=None, use_comoving_dist=False)[source]

Returns diameter [Mpc] of the past lightcone at a given redshift.

Parameters:

  • z (float) – redshift, or comoving distance [Mpc] if use_comoving_dist is True

  • cosmo (astropy cosmology object) – cosmology. If given, replaces the stored cosmology

  • use_comoving_dist (boolean) – If True, then z is passed as a comoving distance from the observer

class swiftlet.snapshot_lightcone.SnapshotLightcone(simulation_object=None, simulation_suite_name=None, boxsize_resolution=None, simulation_name=None, simulation_base_dir_format=None, beam_vector=None, orientation_seed=0, orientation_lock=None, orientation_table=None, verbose=1)[source]

Bases: object

Fundamental code used to construct lightcones from snapshots with SnapshotBeam and SnapshotAllSky sub classes.

Each sub class is built to handle their specific lightcone geometry.

This class tracks:
  1. periodic replications of snapshots and their reorientation

    to avoid exact replication of structures.

  2. reading and placing particles from snapshots into the lightcone

  3. snapshot cosmology

  4. MPI ranks and communication between ranks

The exact methods of identifying particles within the lightcones footprint and how the snapshot box replication occurs is handled in the SnapshotBeam and SnapshotAllSky sub classes.

Define the lightcone’s cosmology, units and vector (where applicable) for the given simulation.

Build a Simulation object from the given simulation suite, boxsize, resolution and simulation name.

Parameters:

  • simulation_suite)name – “flamingo” or “colibre”. If None, found from boxsize_resolution, see simulation_suites.suite_for_label

  • boxsize_resolution (str or Simulation (swiftlet class object)) – box size and resolution label, e.g. “L1000N1800” (FLAMINGO) or “L0200N1504” (COLIBRE), or a Simulation (see swiftlet.simulations), then pass the other arguments by keyword

  • simulation_name (str) – name of the simulation, e.g. “HYDRO_FIDUCIAL”

  • simulation_base_dir_format (str) – directory of the simulation, with {box_res} and {sim_name} fields. If None, the suite’s directory (see simulations.SimulationSuite.directory_format)

  • simulation_object (Simulation, swiftlet Simulation class object) – the simulation, instead of boxsize_resolution and simulation_name

  • beam_vector (numpy.ndarray) – direction vector of the line of sight as an array of 3 floats. None for all-sky

  • orientation_seed (int) – seed used to select the rotation, reflection and periodic shift of each box tile.

  • orientation_lock (str) –

    “none”:

    every box tile has its own orientation.

    ”cube”:

    every box tile in a cube shell of boxes around the observer’s box shares one orientation, so each shell is periodically continuous and theorientation only changes on the faces between shells.

    ”sphere”:

    everything in a spherical shell, between (n-1/2) and (n+1/2) box sidelengths from the observer, shares one orientation, so the orientation only changes at those distances. A box crossing a sphere is used once for each shell, and tiles are labelled (nx, ny, nz, layer)

  • orientation_table (str) – path of an HDF5 file of orientation tables (see snapshot_orientation.write_orientation_tables) to take the quarter turns, reflections and cell shifts of the box tiles from. If None, use the default tables.

lightcone_metadata(redshift_range=None, ang_radius_deg=None)[source]

Returns the lightcone metadata, a dict with the names LIGHTCONE_METADATA_NAMES.

Metadata tracks the settings that made the lightcone and a record of everything placed in it:

  • orientation_seed

  • orientation_lock

  • orientation table (file and fingerprint of its contents) that set the

    orientation of every box tile,

  • the simulation,

  • the beam

  • the redshift range.

Given the same settings and snapshots, the same exact lightcone can be made again.

Parameters:

  • redshift_range (sequence of two floats) – minimum and maximum redshift of the shell placed

  • ang_radius_deg (float) – angular radius [deg] of the beam, None for all-sky

snapshots_for_shell(shell_z, halo_format=None, range_tol=0.0)[source]

Returns the snapshot numbers for the redshift range of the lightcone shell, from low to high redshift.

Read ahead and find which snapshots are available (for particles and SOAP catalogues), then identify which snapshots fill the lightcones redshift range.

If any snapshots are missing, fill the gap in redshft with the neighbouring available snapshots. When filling gaps raise a SnapshotGapWarning.

Raise a ValueError if the redshift spacing between the snapshots is greater than the MAX_SNAPSHOT_SPACING.

Parameters:

  • shell_z (sequence of two floats) – minimum and maximum redshift of the lightcone shell [z_min, z_max]

  • halo_format (str) – see gather_halo_catalogues. If None, the snapshot files are looked for

  • range_tol (float) – a snapshot edge within range_tol of the shell counts as touching it

the number of files found and the list of FileReadSpec entries itself.

Snapshot2Lightcone(snapshot_number, coords, tile=None)[source]

Translate snapshot coordinates into lightcone coordinates for every tile a snapshot supplies to the lightcone.

This function only knows about tiles from the most recently gathered shell and relies on self.last_snapshot_read being populated by either gather_files, place_snapshot_particles_in_shell or the internal _gather_files_for_ptype they both call.

Note: A single snapshot number can supply more than one periodic replica tile to the same shell due to independent rotation, reflection and periodic shifts.

Returns a dict {tile: lightcone_coords}, one entry per tile this snapshot supplies to the last gathered shell.

Parameters:

  • snapshot_number (int) – snapshot number

  • coords (np.ndarray) – comoving snapshot-frame (box) coordinates [Mpc], shape (N, 3)

  • tile (tuple) – a specific periodic replica described by (nx, ny, n_los) for SnapshotBeam or (nx, ny, nz) for SnapshotAllSky. If given, self.last_snapshot_read is not consulted at all, so this works as a standalone method (no gather_files/ place_snapshot_particles_in_shell call needed first). If None, every tile this snapshot supplies to the last-gathered shell is used.

Lightcone2Snapshot(coords, snapshot_number=None, tile=None)[source]

Inverse of Snapshot2Lightcone.

Translate lightcone frame coordinates back into the snapshot numbers and snapshot frame coordinates. This function relies on self.last_snapshot_read and only knows about snapshots and tiles from the most recently gathered shell. Which snapshot a lightcone particle belongs to is determined from its comoving distance alone. Within a matched snapshot the snapshot number alone doesn’t say which of its tiles a given point’s orientation should be inverted to. Therefore, this function inverts every one of that snapshot’s tiles and returns all of them. Only one is the ‘real’ originating tile for any given point .

Returns a dict {snapshot_number: {tile: (point_index, snapshot_coords)}}.
point_index: an integer array indexing into the input coords, i.e., which of the input points

matched the snapshot_number

snapshot_coords: the corresponding snapshot frame coordinates after inverting through tile’s orientation

Note: Points whose comoving distance doesn’t fall inside any recorded snapshot’s range are dropped

Parameters:

  • coords (np.ndarray) – comoving lightcone-frame coordinates [Mpc], shape (N, 3)

  • snapshot_number (int) – skip distance-based snapshot matching and assume every point belongs to this snapshot

  • tile (tuple) – skip tile lookup and invert only through this one tile. Requires snapshot_number to also be given

gather_halo_catalogues(halo_format, shell_z, ang_radius_deg=None, use_snapshots=None, snapshot_number=None)[source]

Halo counterpart of gather_files.

For every snapshot that populates the shell, find the tiles s snapshot is moved into, a done for the particles. The box and cell grid used to move haloes into the tiles are the same in every snapshot, so the cell metadata of only one snapshot is read (snapshot_number).

SOAP catalogues are not sorted by cell, so unlike for particles no cells are selected and every halo of a catalogue is tested.

Each SOAP catalogue to read is recorded with its tile and the tile’s redshift range as a HaloCatalogueSpec. As done for particles, the tiles are also recorded.

Returns self.halo_catalogues_to_read

Parameters:

  • halo_format (str) – format string of the SOAP catalogue filenames, using {snap_nr}

  • shell_z (sequence of two floats) – minimum and maximum redshift of the lightcone shell [z_min, z_max]

  • ang_radius_deg (float) – angular radius [deg] of the beam, ignored if None. Needed by SnapshotBeam and None for SnapshotAllSky.

  • use_snapshots (list or np.ndarray) – snapshot numbers to use instead of the ones auto-selected from shell_z

  • snapshot_number (int) – the snapshot to read the box and cell metadata from. If None, the lowest redshift snapshot used

place_halos_in_shell(halo_format, lightcone_redshift_range, ang_radius_deg=None, use_snapshots=None, soap_chunk_size=None, comm=None, redistribute_halos=False, snapshot_number=None)[source]

Halo counterpart of place_snapshot_particles_in_shell.

Place the haloes of SOAP catalogues in a lightcone shell, exactly as done for the particles. If gather_halo_catalogues has already been called with the same arguments then the first gather pass is not repeated. Then the catalogues are read, and their haloes moved into the lightcone exactly as particles are and kept if they are in the shell.

How the SOAP catalogues are read:

  • in serial (no comm, one MPI rank): soap_chunk_size rows at a time, or each catalogue as a whole if None.

  • with MPI: the catalogues are split into
    pieces of soap_chunk_size rows (if None, each catalogue into one piece per rank), shared between the

    ranks as particle files are. Each rank reads only its own pieces, and returns the haloes it placed. With redistribute_halos, the haloes are then shared evenly between the ranks.

The haloes placed are the same whichever way the catalogues are read (serial or MPI).

Tracks the minimum number of properties needed to look up any other property in the SOAP catalogues later:

  • Lightcone/HaloCentre: the halo’s centre, transformed into the lightcone frame exactly like a particle’s Coordinates.

  • Lightcone/ExpansionFactor: the expansion factor at the halo’s lightcone comoving distance.

  • Lightcone/SnapshotNumber: the snapshot the halo came from.

  • InputHalos/HaloCatalogueIndex: the halo’s index in that snapshot’s SOAP catalogue, as written in it.

  • InputHalos/SOAPIndex: the row of the halo in that snapshot’s SOAP catalogue.

Returns a LightconeOutput of these properties, one row per halo placed.

Parameters:

  • halo_format (str) – format string for SOAP catalogue filenames (using {snap_nr})

  • lightcone_redshift_range (sequence of two floats) – minimum and maximum redshift of the shell to populate [z_min, z_max]

  • ang_radius_deg (float) – angular radius [deg] of the beam, ignored if None. Needed by SnapshotBeam and None for SnapshotAllSky.

  • use_snapshots (list or np.ndarray) – snapshot numbers to use, as in gather_files, bypassing the usual redshift-range lookup

  • soap_chunk_size (int) – number of rows of a SOAP catalogue read at a time. If None, see above

  • comm (mpi4py.MPI.Comm) – MPI communicator. If None, MPI.COMM_WORLD when more than one rank is running, otherwise serial

  • redistribute_halos (boolean) – If True, with MPI, share the haloes placed evenly between the ranks

  • snapshot_number (int) – snapshot to read the box and cell metadata from, see gather_halo_catalogues
